dialogue_quality_notes: Conversation is concise and practical: proposals and responses are short and focused (e.g., A proposes weekends, D accepts).
Some needless repetition of acknowledgements after settlement ('Okay, thanks.' repeated many times in later rounds).
Speakers provide grounded reasons and trade-offs (work-from-home calls, laundry drying times, family food tradition).
Roles and facts remain consistent throughout; no confusion about who said or agreed to what.
evaluation.final_reason: Agents reached a concrete, mutual arrangement by Round 8: Agent D agreed to restrict cooking the strong-smelling dish to weekends ('I can't cook on other nights. I've already agreed with Agent A that I'll only do it on weekends.'), Agent C agreed to shift laundry to a weekend morning so it would be dry before D's usual evening cooking ('If I do it on a weekend morning, it should be dry by the evening. That works.'), and Agent B obtained D's promise to give a heads-up before weekend cooking ('I'll let you know before I start cooking on the weekends.'). All affected parties verbally accepted these terms.
position_change_notes: Agent D moved from resisting change ('I can't really stop cooking it.') to conceding a temporal limit: 'Okay, weekends could work for me.' and later 'I can't cook on other nights... I'll only do it on weekends.'

Agent C shifted from objecting to the notification-only solution ('That doesn't really help me.') to accommodating the agreed weekend plan by changing laundry timing: 'If I do it on a weekend morning... That works.'
Agent A proposed a compromise (weekends) and accepted D's agreement without further concession: 'Yeah, that works for me.'

Agent B consistently sought a smaller accommodation (heads-up) and retained that position until D agreed: 'Can you just give a heads-up before you cook?' — 'I'll let you know before I start cooking on the weekends.'

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 — Agent A: 'When the smell is really strong it hangs around the living room for hours...'; opening request (prior): A had asked that nobody cook strong-smelling food from now on. This raises a potential incompatible demand but no opponent has responded yet.

Turn 3 — Agent C: 'My laundry's in the service yard and it gets the smell too.' Turn 4 — Agent D: '...I can't really stop cooking it.' D's explicit refusal conflicts with A's earlier request, creating a clear substantive incompatibility over cooking practice.

Turn 5 — Agent A: 'How about cooking it on weekends?' Turn 6 — Agent D: 'Okay, weekends could work for me.' A and D move toward a scheduling compromise, reducing but not eliminating other parties' concerns (B/C not yet fully addressed).

Turn 7 — Agent A: 'Yeah, that works for me.' Turn 9 — Agent B: 'The day doesn't really matter for me... Can you just give a heads-up before you cook?' B accepts the weekend idea conditionally (notification), leaving minor outstanding adjustments.
Turn 10 — Agent D: 'Yeah, sure. I can let you know.' Turn 11 — Agent B: 'Okay, thanks.' B's concern (notification) is accepted; C's laundry issue remains unresolved.

Turn 12 — Agent C: 'That doesn't really help me. The laundry's still hanging right there next to the kitchen.' This raises a new practical incompatibility between C's laundry schedule and D's agreed cooking-on-weekends plan. Turn 13 — Agent D: 'You're right. What do you think would work for the laundry?'

Turn 14 — Agent C: 'I do my laundry on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday evenings. Could you cook it on the other nights?' Turn 15 — Agent D: '...I already agreed with Agent A I'd only cook this on weekends. What if you do your laundry on a weekend morning?' D defends the weekend commitment and proposes an alternative, so the disagreement is negotiated but not yet settled.

Turn 18 — Agent D: 'I can't cook on other nights. I've already agreed with Agent A that I'll only do it on weekends.' Turn 19 — Agent C: 'Okay. If I do it on a weekend morning, it should be dry by the evening. That works.' C accepts D's weekend restriction and agrees to shift laundry; substantive incompatibilities are jointly settled.
Turn 20 & Turn 23 — Agent D: 'Okay, good.' No further objections or outstanding incompatibilities are raised; previous settlement stands.
Turn 27 — Agent D: 'Agent B, I'll let you know before I start cooking on the weekends.' Turn 28 — Agent B: 'Okay, thanks.' B's request for notification is confirmed, no outstanding disagreement.
Turn 32 & Turn 36 — Agent B repeats 'Okay, thanks.' These are confirmations after the substantive agreement; no new conflict.
Turn 40 & Turn 44 — Agent B repeats 'Okay, thanks.' Continued acknowledgements; no substantive disagreements introduced.

substantive_insights: Tension was primarily practical: cultural food practice vs shared-space impacts (smell affecting clothes, calls, laundry).
Scheduling (weekend-only cooking) is an effective compromise when structural changes and expenses are off the table.
Notification alone did not solve all problems—laundry location/timing had to be adjusted to eliminate the remaining incompatibility.
Final settlement distributed adjustment across parties: D limited cooking times, C changed laundry timing, B got notifications, A's work concerns were addressed.
